name: Partner visa (subclass 820/801 onshore, 309/100 offshore)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires being the spouse or de facto partner (12+ months cohabitation, or registered relationship) of an Australian citizen, permanent resident, or eligible New Zealand citizen.

This requires the Australian partner to be an approved sponsor, including a character (police) check on the sponsor themselves — a genuinely distinctive requirement not present on most other countries' family routes in this dataset.

evidence_required.document: Extensive relationship evidence (joint finances, cohabitation, social recognition, commitment) — genuinely more evidentiary-intensive than most partner-route requirements in this dataset

outcome.duration_length: temporary stage (820/309) followed by permanent stage (801/100), assessed roughly 2 years after the temporary stage application unless earlier grant criteria are met

sources.title: Partner visa - Department of Home Affairs

notes: PROCESSING-TIME CAVEAT flagged honestly, same class of caveat as Portugal's AIMA backlog and Spain's naturalisation backlog: Australian partner visas are widely reported to face very long real-world processing times, sometimes well beyond 2 years for the permanent-stage decision — the statutory two-stage design (temporary then permanent) doesn't itself specify a hard processing deadline, and the realistic wait was not independently confirmed at a specific tier-1 figure during this research pass, an honest gap rather than a fabricated number. Sponsor-side character check is a genuine structural feature not seen on most other countries' family routes in this dataset — Australia vets the SPONSOR's character, not just the applicant's, worth flagging as a real difference. Two-stage temporary-then-permanent structure (820→801 onshore, 309→100 offshore) is closer to the European partner-visa pattern than Australia's points-tested skilled routes, which grant permanence immediately — a genuine internal inconsistency within Australia's own visa system worth surfacing.
